edges.description: Aberrant lymphatic structures infiltrate bone and adjacent soft tissue.
Bone is resorbed and structurally weakened over time.
Thoracic extension of abnormal lymphatic tissue can disrupt pleural lymphatic drainage.
Active osteolysis commonly causes localized pain.
Osteoclast-mediated bone resorption produces progressive disappearing bone lesions.
Progressive cortical and trabecular bone loss weakens bone structure and predisposes to pathological fractures.
Thoracic lymphatic disruption can produce chylous pleural effusions.
Skeletal pain state manifests clinically as localized bone pain.
Accumulation of chylous effusion in the pleural cavity manifests clinically as chylothorax.
